claims.text: The route spans from the medieval heights of Eze Village to the coastal Saint-Tropez Citadel, covering approximately 89 km of diverse terrain.
This journey unveils the Riviera's dual identity: from the fairytale views of Èze perched over 400m above sea level to Monaco's royal beginnings under Prince Charles III Grimaldi.

The opulent villas of Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat draw a luxurious contrast to the historic Citadelle of Saint-Tropez, erected in the early 1600s for coastal defense, attracting artists like Paul Signac in a tale of protection and artistic inspiration.
In the upcoming stops, you will learn about Laurent Fignon's crash in 1989 at Eze Village and the unexpected incident involving Peter Sagan in May 2023 in Monaco.
These stories will be complemented by the historical significance of the Cap Ferrat Coastal Path as a former customs route.
From Nice, take the train to Eze-sur-Mer station, then bike uphill on D6098 for about 4 km to reach Eze Village.
The narrow, cobblestone streets wind upwards, leading to breathtaking views at over 400 meters above sea level.
Èze Village is a remarkable stop o biking tour, not just for its mesmerizing views, but also for its rich history and connection to the world of cycling.
In 1989, the Paris–Nice race, a prestigious event in the cycling calendar, saw French cycling legend Laurent Fignon crash on the descent near Èze.
claims.evidence: In 1989, French cycling legend Laurent Fignon crashed on the descent near Èze during the Paris–Nice race but managed to win the overall victory by fractions of a second.

claims.text: Despite this setback, Fignon's determination led him to secure the overall victory by just fractions of a second.
In more recent times, the 2012 Paris–Nice race added another chapter to Èze's cycling legacy.
British cyclist Bradley Wiggins faced dense sea fog during the climb past Èze.
claims.evidence: In 2012, Bradley Wiggins held off Lieuwe Westra by eight seconds to win the Paris–Nice race, despite dense sea fog during the climb past Èze.

claims.text: In a display of skill and resilience, Wiggins managed to hold off his competitor, Lieuwe Westra, by a mere eight seconds, clinching the victory.
These stories of triumph and endurance echo through the winding streets, where modern-day cycling stars like Tadej Pogačar, Geraint Thomas, and Remco Evenepoel frequently train.
The village itself, first populated around 200 BC near Mount Bastide, offers a journey through time.
The best viewing position here is at the iconic Casino de Monte-Carlo, where you can take in the opulent architecture and the bustling life around the square.
Step into Monaco, a principality that stands as a semi-enclave within, enveloped by France on three sides and overlooking the shimmering Mediterranean.
The casino's gilded halls have witnessed fortunes made and lost, encapsulating the sense of drama that Monaco is known for.
In May 2023, the renowned cyclist Peter Sagan found himself at the center of an unexpected incident in Monaco.
While attempting to park a scooter, Sagan was caught by the police in an intoxicated state.
claims.evidence: In May 2023, Peter Sagan was caught by Monaco police trying to park a scooter while heavily intoxicated, resulting in a three-month suspended prison sentence and a suspended driving license.

claims.text: This episode adds to Monaco's tapestry of high-profile stories, underscoring how even the most celebrated individuals can find themselves entwined with the principality’s legal net.
In the late 1990s and early 2000s, Lance Armstrong famously used the nearby Col de la Madone as a performance benchmark.
claims.evidence: Lance Armstrong used the Col de la Madone as a performance benchmark during the late 1990s and early 2000s, believing a climb under 31 minutes indicated readiness to win the Tour de France.

claims.text: Completing the climb in under 31 minutes was considered an indication of readiness to win the Tour de France.
claims.evidence: Lance Armstrong used the Col de la Madone as a performance benchmark during the late 1990s and early 2000s, believing a climb under 31 minutes indicated readiness to win the Tour de France.

claims.text: This climb has become a symbol of ambition and endurance, resonating with the aspirations that Monaco embodies.
The Cap Ferrat Coastal Path has more than just scenic beauty; it is woven with tales of intrigue and history.
In the 18th and 19th centuries, this path was a lifeline for French customs officers tasked with patrolling against Mediterranean smugglers.
Nearby, a glimpse of Villa Les Cèdres offers another chapter of Cap Ferrat's storied history.
In 1900, King Leopold II of Belgium purchased this grand villa to house his young companion, Blanche Zélia Joséphine Delacroix, known as Caroline Lacroix.
Their relationship, and eventual marriage in 1909, caused quite an uproar, both diplomatically and within the royal family.
As Leopold lay on his deathbed, he sought to secure Caroline’s inheritance through a religious ceremony, ensuring her place in history and tying her fate to this breathtaking locale.
Further along, the presence of Villa Santo Sospir sheds light on the artistic flair of the region.
In 1950, the villa became a canvas for artist Jean Cocteau.
Over a decade, Cocteau adorned its walls with frescoes inspired by pagan and mythological themes, transforming the villa into a living gallery.
On August 15, 1944, amid the cacophony of war, the Citadel witnessed a pivotal moment during Operation Dragoon, the code name for the Allied invasion.
Allied forces advanced, prompting the German garrison stationed here to raise the white flag.
The Citadel has witnessed cultural mingling tales.
Today, within these ancient walls, the Citadel houses a maritime museum, showcasing the town's transition from a fortified stronghold to a cultural haven.
